claims.title: Empirical conditioning gap identifies weak preference regions
claims.known: GPI-LS prioritizes weight vectors with a formal GPI lower-bound signal; PGMORL predicts policy-task improvement; C-MORL allocates search toward sparse Pareto regions.
claims.difference: This repository ranks preferences by an empirical archive-relative conditioning gap of one shared conditioned policy rather than a GPI bound, policy-performance predictor, or crowding distance.
claims.falsifier: A prior method that uses the same archive-relative scalarization gap to schedule updates for one preference-conditioned policy, or evidence that the score adds no predictive value over the closest antecedent.
claims.differentiating_experiment: Correlate the score at time t with held-out future utility improvement at t+k.
claims.allowed_wording: The repository implements an empirical conditioning-gap allocation signal; predictive value is unvalidated.

claims.title: Masked-ensemble disagreement identifies useful allocation regions
claims.known: Value Disagreement Sampling uses ensemble value dispersion as an epistemic-uncertainty curriculum signal for goal selection.
claims.difference: The repository transfers disagreement sampling to preference candidates and estimates it with shared masked heads; that construction is cheaper but is not yet calibrated as epistemic uncertainty.
claims.falsifier: A prior preference-conditioned MORL system with materially equivalent masked-head disagreement allocation, or failed calibration and future-improvement tests against matched random sampling.
claims.differentiating_experiment: Measure uncertainty calibration and future-improvement correlation against compute-matched random allocation.
claims.allowed_wording: Masked head disagreement is implemented as a candidate allocation signal, not established epistemic uncertainty.

claims.title: Local coverage and recency improve preference allocation
claims.known: Prioritized Level Replay explicitly mixes a learning-potential score with staleness; C-MORL uses crowding distance to target sparse Pareto-front regions.
claims.difference: The implementation combines local preference-simplex coverage with per-candidate recency inside a conditioned-MORL sampler.
claims.falsifier: A prior preference sampler with the same local-coverage and recency construction, or ablations showing neither component improves allocation under matched budgets.
claims.differentiating_experiment: Compare coverage-only and recency-aware variants across pool size and front geometry.
claims.allowed_wording: The sampler includes local coverage and recency signals whose empirical benefit remains unknown.

claims.title: Observed learning progress is a better allocation target than difficulty or uncertainty
claims.known: ALP-GMM and CURIOUS allocate curriculum probability using absolute learning progress; GPI-LS prioritizes weights using a bound connected to expected improvement.
claims.difference: The proposed study estimates lagged progress over preference regions and directly compares its predictive value with gap, disagreement, coverage/recency, uniform, and matched-random signals.
claims.falsifier: A prior controlled preference-MORL study making the same predictive comparison, or evidence that lagged progress does not predict or cause future improvement beyond controls.
claims.differentiating_experiment: Compare lagged progress-only allocation with gap-only, disagreement-only, and matched random controls.
claims.allowed_wording: We test whether observed learning progress is more predictive than difficulty or disagreement.

claims.title: Combining gap, disagreement, coverage/recency, and progress improves sample efficiency
claims.known: Adaptive curricula already combine notions of difficulty, improvement potential, uncertainty, diversity, and staleness in adjacent settings; CAPQL also establishes conditioned continuous-control MORL over a fixed weight distribution.
claims.difference: The contribution would be a controlled factorial comparison of four familiar outcome-dependent allocation signals within one conditioned-MORL implementation, not a wholly new signal family or conditioned architecture.
claims.falsifier: A prior factorial study with the same signals and controls, or paired experiments showing the combination is no better than uniform or compute-matched random allocation.
claims.differentiating_experiment: Run every signal-only, pairwise, full, uniform, and compute-matched random ablation under paired seeds.
claims.allowed_wording: The study evaluates a combined allocation rule assembled from familiar signals; no novelty or superiority is claimed yet.

claims.title: Adaptive preference allocation affects robustness under dynamics shift
claims.known: MORL-Generalization already formalizes generalization across contexts and environments and separates those axes from preference-conditioned objectives.
claims.difference: The repository asks whether adaptive preference allocation changes robustness under predeclared dynamics shifts while treating unseen-preference and environment generalization as distinct claims.
claims.falsifier: A prior matched-budget study of adaptive preference allocation under equivalent dynamics shifts, or locked-checkpoint evaluations showing no robust difference from controls.
claims.differentiating_experiment: Evaluate locked checkpoints on nominal and predeclared OOD shifts without using OOD test results for tuning.
claims.allowed_wording: Environment-shift robustness is a separate evaluation question from unseen-preference generalization.
